title: SQL Fundamentals
intro: SQL interview questions for freshers are asked at almost every Python backend interview regardless of experience level — because every backend developer eventually needs to write a query. This page covers SELECT with WHERE, ORDER BY, and LIMIT (the 80% of SQL you'll write every day), the JOIN types every interviewer probes (INNER JOIN, LEFT JOIN, RIGHT JOIN — with a diagram-style explanation of what rows each one includes), GROUP BY with aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN — and the WHERE vs HAVING distinction that trips up most freshers), subqueries (when a SELECT result becomes the input to another SELECT), primary and foreign key constraints, and the index concept (why adding an index makes SELECT fast but INSERT slower — the trade-off question that separates candidates who understand databases from candidates who have only run queries). Every SQL example uses a simple two-table schema (orders and customers) so the join logic is clear.
